chapters.title: The Law of Burnt Offerings
chapters.synopsis: The Lord calls to Moses from the tabernacle and gives instructions for burnt offerings from the herd, the flock, and the fowls. Each offering is wholly consumed on the altar as a voluntary act of devotion and atonement.

chapters.title: The Offering of Fine Flour
chapters.synopsis: The Lord prescribes meat offerings of fine flour with oil and frankincense, baked or fried. No leaven or honey may be burned, and every offering must be seasoned with salt, the token of the covenant.

chapters.title: Peace Offerings Before the Lord
chapters.synopsis: The Lord gives the law of peace offerings taken from the herd or the flock. The fat is burned upon the altar, and Israel is commanded to eat neither fat nor blood.

chapters.title: Offerings for Sins of Ignorance
chapters.synopsis: The Lord sets out sin offerings for priests, for the whole congregation, for rulers, and for common people who sin through ignorance. When the offering is made, the sin is forgiven.

chapters.title: Trespass Offerings and Confession
chapters.synopsis: The Lord requires confession and a trespass offering for hidden sins, rash oaths, and touching unclean things. The poor may bring turtledoves or fine flour, so that atonement is within reach of all.

chapters.title: Continual Fire Upon the Altar
chapters.synopsis: The Lord commands restitution plus a fifth part for trespass against a neighbor. He gives the priests the laws of the burnt, meat, and sin offerings, and the fire on the altar must never go out.

chapters.title: Laws of the Priests' Portions
chapters.synopsis: The Lord completes the laws of the trespass and peace offerings, including thanksgiving offerings. The priests receive their appointed portions, and eating fat or blood is strictly forbidden.

chapters.title: Aaron and His Sons Consecrated
chapters.synopsis: Moses washes, clothes, and anoints Aaron and his sons before the congregation, consecrating them to the priesthood as the Lord commanded. They remain at the tabernacle door seven days to fulfil their consecration.

chapters.title: The Glory of the Lord Appears
chapters.synopsis: On the eighth day Aaron offers the first sacrifices for himself and for the people, and blesses them. The glory of the Lord appears, and fire from the Lord consumes the offering on the altar.

chapters.title: Strange Fire Before the Lord
chapters.synopsis: Nadab and Abihu, sons of Aaron, offer strange fire and are consumed by fire from the Lord. Priests are forbidden wine when serving, and Moses instructs Aaron's remaining sons in their sacred duties.

chapters.title: Clean and Unclean Meats
chapters.synopsis: The Lord distinguishes the beasts, fish, fowls, and creeping things that Israel may and may not eat. The people are to sanctify themselves and be holy, for the Lord is holy.

chapters.title: Purification After Childbirth
chapters.synopsis: The Lord gives the days of purification for a mother after the birth of a son or a daughter. She then brings a burnt offering and a sin offering, or two doves if she is poor.

chapters.title: Discerning the Plague of Leprosy
chapters.synopsis: The Lord teaches the priests how to examine skin diseases and pronounce a person clean or unclean. Lepers must dwell apart outside the camp, and garments with the plague are burned.

chapters.title: Cleansing the Healed Leper
chapters.synopsis: The Lord prescribes the rites for cleansing a healed leper, using two birds, cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop, with offerings on the eighth day. He also gives the law for leprosy found in a house.

chapters.title: Laws of Bodily Issues
chapters.synopsis: The Lord declares the uncleanness caused by bodily issues in men and women and the washings required. Israel must be separated from uncleanness so the tabernacle among them is not defiled.

chapters.title: The Day of Atonement
chapters.synopsis: The Lord appoints one day each year when Aaron enters the holy place with blood to make atonement for himself and all Israel. A scapegoat bears the sins of the people into the wilderness.

chapters.title: The Life Is in the Blood
chapters.synopsis: The Lord commands that sacrifices be brought only to the tabernacle door and forbids offerings to devils. Eating blood is forbidden, for the life of the flesh is in the blood, given to make atonement.

chapters.title: Walk Not in Their Ordinances
chapters.synopsis: The Lord forbids Israel to follow the practices of Egypt and Canaan, listing unlawful marriages and relations. Such abominations defiled the land before them, and Israel must keep the Lord's statutes and live.

chapters.title: Ye Shall Be Holy
chapters.synopsis: The Lord commands Israel to be holy as he is holy, gathering laws of honesty, justice, care for the poor and the stranger, and love of neighbor. Every command rests on the refrain, I am the Lord.

segments.speaker: the-lord
segments.note: laws of holiness and neighborly love

chapters.title: Penalties for Defilement
chapters.synopsis: The Lord fixes penalties for giving children to Molech, turning to familiar spirits, and unlawful relations. Israel is severed from other peoples to be holy unto the Lord.

chapters.title: The Holiness of the Priests
chapters.synopsis: The Lord sets stricter standards for priests concerning mourning, marriage, and bodily blemish. Those who offer the bread of their God must be holy and without profaning his sanctuaries.

chapters.title: Holy Things Kept Holy
chapters.synopsis: The Lord instructs the priests to keep themselves clean before eating the holy offerings and states who in a priest's house may eat them. Every sacrifice brought to the Lord must be without blemish.

chapters.title: The Feasts of the Lord
chapters.synopsis: The Lord appoints his holy convocations: the sabbath, passover and unleavened bread, firstfruits, pentecost, trumpets, the day of atonement, and the feast of tabernacles. Each feast is a statute for ever throughout Israel's generations.

chapters.title: The Lamps, Bread, and Blasphemer
chapters.synopsis: The Lord commands pure oil for the continual lamps and twelve loaves of shewbread set weekly before him. A man who blasphemes the name of the Lord is judged and stoned, and the law of just recompense is given.

chapters.title: Sabbath Years and the Jubilee
chapters.synopsis: The Lord ordains a sabbath rest for the land every seventh year and a jubilee every fiftieth, when land returns to its family and Israelite servants go free. The land is the Lord's, and his people are not to oppress one another.

chapters.title: Blessings and Cursings Declared
chapters.synopsis: The Lord promises rain, peace, and his presence if Israel keeps his commandments, and warns of terror, famine, and scattering if they do not. Yet if they confess and humble themselves, he will remember his covenant.

chapters.title: Vows, Devotions, and Tithes
chapters.synopsis: The Lord gives the valuations for persons, animals, houses, and fields devoted by vow, and the rules for redeeming them. The tithe of the land and of the flock is holy unto the Lord.
